title: Agent
description: Configures a complete voice AI agent by wiring together STT → LLM → TTS with integrated turn detection. Provides a higher-level abstraction than manually orchestrating the individual components. Optimized for building voice AI agents with proper turn-taking behavior.

id.description: An optional unique identifier for this verb instance.

autoLockLanguage.description: Switch the TTS to the language the caller speaks, using the matching languageConfig entry. Works with any STT that reports the detected language: Deepgram (language 'multi', or Flux Multilingual), AssemblyAI (languageDetection), Google and Azure (altLanguages), Soniox (enableLanguageIdentification), Gladia and Modulate. Values: false (disabled), true (lock on the first utterance whose language is detected), 'always' (re-evaluate every turn). With Deepgram Flux, true also locks the STT language hints to the detected language. Default: false.

languageConfig.description: Per-language TTS overrides, used when autoLockLanguage detects a language. Keys are language codes such as 'es' or 'es-MX'. A detected language matches an exact key first (case-insensitive), then a key with the same primary language, so 'es' matches a detected 'es-US'. A detected language with no entry keeps the current TTS. The entry's tts is merged over the agent's tts; set its language to the code the TTS vendor expects.

tts.description: TTS config override for this language. Merged with default tts.

oneOf.description: Turn detection strategy shorthand. 'stt' uses the STT vendor's native signals (silence-based for most vendors; acoustic+semantic for deepgramflux, assemblyai, speechmatics). 'krisp' uses the Krisp acoustic end-of-turn model with default settings.
Turn detection configuration with tunable parameters.

mode.description: Turn detection mode. Currently only 'krisp' supports object-form tuning.

threshold.description: Krisp end-of-turn confidence threshold (0.0–1.0). Lower values trigger earlier turn transitions. Default: 0.5

turnDetection.description: Turn detection strategy. Controls when the agent decides the user has finished speaking. STT vendors with native turn-taking (deepgramflux, assemblyai, speechmatics) always use their built-in detection regardless of this setting.

bargeIn.description: Controls whether and how the user can interrupt the assistant while it is speaking.

enable.description: Allow the user to interrupt the assistant while it is speaking. Default: true.

strategy.description: How interruptions are detected. 'vad' (default): speech onset tentatively interrupts the assistant and is confirmed after minSpeechDuration of sustained speech, otherwise the assistant resumes. 'interruptPrediction': an ML model scores whether caller speech is a genuine interruption attempt vs backchannel (e.g. 'uh-huh'), so the assistant is never tentatively paused and backchannel does not cut it off; requires a provisioned vendor API key.

vendor.description: Detection vendor for strategy 'interruptPrediction'; defaults to 'krisp' (currently the only option). Not used with strategy 'vad'.

threshold.description: Probability threshold for interruptPrediction (0-1). Higher values require stronger evidence before interrupting the assistant. Default: 0.5.

minSpeechDuration.description: Seconds of detected speech required before confirming an interruption. Prevents brief noises from cutting off the assistant. Applies to strategy 'vad' only. Default: 0.5

sticky.description: If true, once the user interrupts the assistant does not resume speaking. Default: false.

noResponseTimeout.description: Seconds to wait after the assistant finishes speaking before prompting the user to respond. 0 disables. Default: 12.

noResponseMaxPrompts.description: End the agent after this many no-response prompts in a row get no reply. The actionHook then fires with completionReason 'no_response', so the application decides what happens next. The count resets whenever the user speaks. 0 or unset: no limit (the agent keeps prompting). Requires feature-server with jambonz/feature-server#259.

llm.description: LLM configuration for the agent. Optional: when omitted, or when `vendor`/`model` are omitted, they fall back to the application's configured default LLM (like `stt`/`tts`). With `vendor: "harness"` a customer-run harness decides what to say instead of a model, over one WebSocket per call opened by jambonz; jambonz keeps STT, turn-taking, barge-in and TTS. See `harness`.

vendor.description: LLM vendor id. Must match a `@jambonz/llm` registered adapter, or be "harness" for a customer-run harness (the account's Harness credential, looked up by vendor and label, gives its WebSocket URL and key). Optional: falls back to the application's default LLM vendor.

model.description: Vendor-specific model id (e.g. 'gpt-4o', 'claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929'). Optional: falls back to the application's default LLM model.

label.description: Optional label to disambiguate when the account has multiple credentials for the same vendor. null or omitted selects the unlabelled credential.

auth.description: Optional inline credentials. When omitted, feature-server looks up credentials by (vendor, label) from the database.

systemPrompt.description: System prompt for the model. Placed vendor-appropriately (top-level for Anthropic/Bedrock, config.systemInstruction for Gemini, role:'system' for OpenAI-compatibles).

messages.description: Seed conversation history. A role:'system' entry is extracted into systemPrompt internally.

maxTokens.description: Maximum tokens the model may generate per turn.

reasoningEffort.description: Deprecated: has no effect. Accepted so existing applications keep validating. To control thinking, set the vendor's own parameter in vendorParams, e.g. {"reasoning_effort": "none"} for openai, {"thinkingConfig": {"thinkingLevel": "minimal"}} for google, {"thinking": {"type": "disabled"}} for deepseek, {"reasoning": {"effort": "minimal"}} for openrouter.

vendorParams.description: Vendor-specific request parameters, passed through as-is. Fields are added to the vendor request (the request body for OpenAI-compatible vendors such as openai and openrouter, the generation config for google and vertex-gemini) but never override a field jambonz sets itself (model, messages, tools, max tokens, temperature, ...). Not validated by jambonz; ignored by anthropic and bedrock. Example for openrouter: {"provider": {"sort": "latency"}, "models": ["openai/gpt-4.1-mini"]}.

tools.description: Tool / function definitions available to the model. The MCP-flat shape `{name, description, parameters}` is canonical; the OpenAI-wrapped form `{type:'function', function:{...}}` is also accepted. With vendor "harness" these are sent to the harness in session:start as OpenAI function definitions, and the harness runs them with tool:call through the toolHook.

harness.description: Harness settings, only with vendor "harness". The harness owns prompts, context, fillers and reprompts, so with it `llmOptions` may carry only `tools`, `model`/`auth`/`connectOptions` are not allowed, and `mcpServers`, `toolFiller`, `earlyGeneration`, `speechCleanup: true` and `noResponseMaxPrompts` are rejected. `noResponseTimeout` still sets when the harness is sent a `silence` event; jambonz does not reprompt on its own. `handoff`, when present, supplies the defaults (mode, disposition, timeout, callerId) for transfers the harness asks for.

url.description: The harness's WebSocket URL (wss://, or ws:// for a private address). When given it is used instead of the url in the Harness credential, and the credential, chosen by `label`, is needed only for its key: with no `label` and no unlabelled Harness credential the socket opens without an Authorization header.

metadata.description: Free-form JSON passed to the harness in session:start (for example agent id, version and per-call variables).

firstChunkTimeoutMs.description: Milliseconds from the end of the caller's turn to the harness's first reply:chunk (or reply:done). On the first timeout holdingPhrase is spoken once; on a second timeout onHarnessFailure runs. While a tool:call from the harness is outstanding, the second timeout waits for it. Default: 4000.

holdingPhrase.description: Spoken once when the harness has not started its reply within firstChunkTimeoutMs, for example 'One moment.'. When omitted nothing is spoken and the second timeout still applies.

onHarnessFailure.description: What jambonz does when the harness cannot be reached, stops answering, or drops and cannot be reconnected within 2 seconds: speak `say`, then transfer to `transfer` if given, otherwise hang up. The actionHook reports completionReason 'harness_failure' with a harness_error object.

say.description: Spoken to the caller before the transfer or hangup.

transfer.description: Where to transfer the caller: an E.164 number, a sip: URI, or a registered user name. Uses the verb's `handoff` settings when present, otherwise a blind transfer by dial.

actionHook.description: A webhook invoked when the agent ends.

eventHook.description: A webhook invoked for agent events. Receives event types: 'user_transcript' (user speech recognized), 'llm_response' (assistant reply), 'user_interruption' (barge-in detected), and 'turn_end' (end-of-turn summary with transcript, response, and latency metrics). With vendor "harness" it also receives 'harness_failure' ({reason, message}) when onHarnessFailure runs, and turn_end carries `engine: "harness"`, `harness.turn_record` and `latency.harness_first_chunk_ms`.

toolHook.description: A webhook invoked when the LLM requests a tool/function call. The payload includes the tool name and arguments; the response provides the tool result.

greeting.description: Whether the LLM should generate an initial greeting before the user speaks. Default: true.

earlyGeneration.description: Enable speculative LLM prompting before end-of-turn is confirmed. When using Krisp turn detection, set this to true to speculatively prompt the LLM before Krisp confirms the turn has ended. If the transcript matches when turn ends, buffered tokens are released immediately — reducing response latency. Note: Deepgram Flux performs early generation automatically via its native EagerEndOfTurn signal regardless of this setting. Default: false.

speak.description: Whether the agent's text is spoken. With false the agent never talks (for example while it drives a DTMF-only phone menu with its tools): the LLM's text is still kept in conversation history, llm_response events and the transcript, but is never sent to TTS, and toolFiller and earlyGeneration are turned off. Each reply ends when the LLM finishes, as for a reply that only called tools. Default: true.

speechCleanup.description: Keep text the model was not meant to say out of TTS: a paragraph that is only a stage direction in (), [] or ** (such as '(silence)' or '[No response needed]'), and <think>, <thinking> or <reasoning> blocks. Asides inside a sentence are still spoken. Applied as the reply streams; ordinary speech is not delayed. A reply with nothing left to say ends without speaking. History, llm_response events and the transcript keep the model's raw text. Default: true.

oneOf.description: Shorthand — enable noise isolation with the specified vendor using default settings.

label.description: Label of the speech credential to use, for vendors that need one (kugelaudio).

auth.description: Optional inline credentials for vendors that need them (kugelaudio). When omitted, feature-server looks up the speech credential by (vendor, label).

direction.description: Audio direction to apply noise isolation. 'read' filters caller audio, 'write' filters outbound audio. Default: 'read'.

noiseIsolation.description: Enable server-side noise isolation to reduce background noise on call audio. Defaults to filtering inbound (caller) audio; set direction to 'write' for outbound. Useful for improving STT accuracy in noisy environments.

url.description: The URL of the MCP server.

mcpServers.description: External MCP servers that provide tools to the LLM. The agent connects at startup via SSE, discovers available tools, and makes them callable by the LLM.

handoff.description: Declarative transfer-to-human config. When present, the runtime injects a 'transfer_to_human' tool into the agent's toolset and runs the packaged transfer choreography (blind/warm) when the LLM calls it.

hangup.description: Enable the built-in hangup tool. When present, the runtime injects a 'hangup' tool into the agent's toolset; when the LLM calls it, the call is ended with a reason placed in an X-Reason SIP header (LLM-supplied reason wins, falling back to hangup.reason).

toolFiller.description: Configuration for playing filler audio while tool calls are in progress. Prevents silence during long-running tool executions.

llmMessage.description: A conversation-history message. The library normalizes content to a string; adapters may carry vendor-native shapes internally.

type.description: Filler mode. 'audio' plays a looping audio file (killed immediately when tool returns). 'backchannel' uses TTS to speak short phrases like 'one moment...' or 'checking that...' (allowed to complete before next action).

startDelaySecs.description: Seconds to wait after tool invocation before playing filler. Prevents filler on fast tools. Default: 2

url.description: Audio file URL (for type='audio'). Should be loopable. Playback stops immediately when tool returns.

style.description: Free-form style hint for LLM-generated phrases (for type='backchannel'). Examples: 'casual', 'professional', 'friendly and patient'. The LLM interprets this when generating filler phrases at call start.

escalationSecs.description: Seconds from tool invocation before generating a longer explanatory response (for type='backchannel'). Useful for tools that may take 10+ seconds. Default: 10

messages.content: You are a helpful voice assistant.
You are a helpful voice assistant.

tools.name: lookup_account
tools.description: Look up the caller's account by phone number.

onHarnessFailure.say: Sorry, I'm having trouble. Transferring you now.
